title: Hybrid occupancy+latency targeting scaler with discrete steps and soft rollback
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and implement a hybrid autoscaling policy engine variant that composes token-occupancy, concurrent-requests, and latency-percentile signals into a single target with discrete scaling steps and a soft rollback/orchestrated fallback path. This ticket covers spec, simulation, control loop implementation in the scaling orchestration layer, safety limits, and integration tests for Dedicated GPU fleets. The goal is to reduce overprovisioning during token-heavy workloads while preserving tail-latency SLOs and enabling predictable tenant billing. Key ideas: 1) Build a composite target metric T = max(W_occ * occ_norm, W_q95 * q95_norm, W_cr * cr_norm) where occ_norm is token occupancy normalized per-SKU, q95_norm is q95/target_q95, cr_norm is concurrent_requests/target_cr. 2) Use a hybrid controller: small discrete non-linear stepper for large deltas (fast response up to a configured headroom limit) and a latency-weighted proportional-integral (PI) controller for fine-grained adjustments. 3) Safety envelope: per-tenant hard min/max nodes, slew-rate caps (nodes per minute), bankruptcy credit bucket for emergency bursts, and a rollout-aware cool-down tied to model-variant fallbacks. 4) Soft rollback: when the controller detects sustained quality regressions or model OOMs, automatically apply a staged rollback to previous capacity with an orchestrated traffic diversion to fallback model variants while keeping a safe reserve for retries. 5) Telemetry: surface per-tenant contribution to target metric, headroom utilization, decision trace (why we scaled), and simulated cost delta in Console and runtime traces.
acceptance_criteria: Spec document reviewed and approved by Runtime and Product (design decisions and safety envelope)
Controller implemented in orchestration service with feature flag and end-to-end tests
Simulation results showing >=15% reduction in steady-state nodes for token-heavy synthetic workloads without >5% increase in p95 latency
Integration test that validates slew-rate caps, per-tenant min/max and emergency credit consumption
Console charting for composite target, decision trace, and per-tenant headroom exposed in runtime-1.20 release
PRs merged with green CI and a canary rollout plan (including rollback playbook)

implementation_notes: Normalization: use rolling window 5m median for occupancy and exp-weighted mean for concurrent requests
Discrete stepper: exponential backoff on repeated upscales within cool-down window to avoid cascade
PI controller: anti-windup via clamping tied to hard max nodes and credit bucket
Fallback orchestration: integrate with model routing to divert % traffic to cheaper model-variants on capacity constraint
Telemetry: emit decision_trace with input vector and chosen subcontroller (discrete|PI)
